findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with just `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data. This class implements none of them, so `Detector.detector_handler` calling `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for a metric_alert_fire detector raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, and process_detectors crashes instead of the previous no-op behaviour where evaluate() returned []. Implement stub versions of the abstract methods, provide defaults in StatefulDetectorHandler, or keep this placeholder on DetectorHandler until it is implemented.

findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence for the wrong group key
findings.body: The expected occurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...), so its fingerprint is [<detector_id>:val1], but evaluate_group_key_value is then called with group_key "group_key" and value 10, so the handler builds an occurrence with fingerprint [<detector_id>:group_key]. IssueOccurrence equality includes the fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the actual result and this test fails / does not verify the intended dedupe path. Build the expected occurrence with "group_key" (and the value actually passed, 10).

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring says evaluate "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult", but this PR changes the signature and implementation to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Implementers relying on the docstring will implement or consume the wrong return type; update the docstring to describe the dict keyed by group_key.
